hypotheses.construction_plan: Define a generic two-argument evaluation K(a,b). The first branch is obtained by substituting a=n, b=m. The second branch is obtained by specializing the second argument to equal the first (b=a), then substituting a=n; equivalently, instantiate the template at (a,b)=(n,n). The piecewise expression selects between these two instances based on whether n and m are unequal.
required_assumptions: K is defined on the domain containing (n,m) and (n,n); parameter substitution is valid.
hypotheses.rationale: The two non-identical branch expressions are evaluations of the same binary kernel K. The second is the diagonal specialization of the first under the identification m=n, so both branches are instances of a shared parameterized object K(a,b).
